layout.arrangement: Horizontal stacked bands: a light-gray title band across the very top with a centered dark-red bold title; a full-width pale-yellow text box directly below holding a two-line paragraph; a large white panel with a thin red border fills the lower ~55% of the slide and contains one wide hand-drawn CNN diagram (orange input slab on the left, stack of colored filter slabs in the center, tan output cube on the right) with handwritten annotations and a red equation at the bottom-left; a thin black video-player bar sits at the very bottom edge.

regions.name: Title band
regions.content: Centered bold dark-red title 'How many filter can we apply on the image' on a light-gray background

regions.name: Explanation text box
regions.position: upper-middle, full width with ~2% side margins, ~24-45% height
regions.content: Pale-yellow box with a black serif paragraph; 'multiple filters' bold black, 'same location' bold dark-red, 'detect edges/lines/curves' bold black

regions.name: Diagram panel
regions.content: White area with thin red border containing the hand-drawn convolution-depth diagram, handwritten labels (RGB, 3 dims, 7, 7, 5, 3, =, Depth=5 dims), the question 'How many weights for these 5 neurons?' and the red equation '5 · 7 · 7 · 3 = 735'

regions.name: Video-player bar
regions.content: Solid black strip (player progress bar, not slide content)

layout.hierarchy: The title dominates as the largest/heaviest text (bold, dark red, ~32pt, centered). The body paragraph is secondary (~20pt black with red bold highlights). The diagram occupies the most area but its handwritten labels are small; the red equation at bottom-left is a strong focal accent.

visual_elements.description: Input image slab: a hand-drawn 3D rectangular slab (the RGB input image) in perspective, orange/brown fill with darker orange edges; handwritten label 'RGB' above it; '3 dims' to its left with a tiny arrow pointing at the slab; a small hand-drawn circle containing an 'X' marks a pixel on the slab face; two handwritten '7' labels with small arrows mark the 7x7 patch extent (one at the left edge of the dashed region, one below-left); several horizontal dashed black lines run from the slab rightward toward the filter stack representing the receptive-field column.
visual_elements.position: left side of diagram panel, ~15-30% x, ~50-80% y

visual_elements.description: Filter stack: a cluster of overlapping hand-drawn 3D slabs (the 5 filters) arranged left-to-right; front row of five slabs colored cyan-blue, green, red, yellow, purple; additional partially hidden slabs peek out behind them in tan, light gray and dark navy; handwritten '5' with a small pointer sits above the stack and handwritten '3' below it (each filter is 7x7x3); dashed lines connect the stack back to the input slab.
visual_elements.position: center of diagram panel, ~30-55% x, ~50-78% y

visual_elements.description: Output volume: a large hand-drawn 3D cube in tan/burlywood with slightly darker top and side faces; a row of 5 circles is drawn along its top face (left to right: tan, tan, tan, dark brown, green) and 5 circles on its front face (left to right: teal, green, red, yellow, purple), one per filter output; handwritten label 'Depth=5 dims' at its upper right; a plain black horizontal arrow at the cube's upper left points rightward into the cube.
visual_elements.position: right side of diagram panel, ~54-82% x, ~50-85% y

visual_elements.description: A large '=' sign placed between the filter stack and the output cube, indicating the 5 filters produce the depth-5 output volume.
visual_elements.position: between filter stack and cube, ~51-54% x, ~63-68% y

visual_elements.description: Handwritten-style black question 'How many weights for these 5 neurons?' with the answer directly below in red: '5 · 7 · 7 · 3 = 735' (5 filters times 7x7 spatial size times 3 input channels equals 735 weights).
visual_elements.position: bottom-left of diagram panel, ~7-45% x, ~83-95% y

imagery: No photographs or clip-art; the only imagery is the sketch/hand-drawn marker-style 3D diagram (orange input slab, colored filter slabs, tan output cube with colored circles) inside the red-bordered panel, resembling a whiteboard illustration.
typography_notes: Title: bold sans-serif (Arial/Calibri-like), ~32-34pt, dark red, centered, sentence case (no all-caps; note the verbatim singular 'filter'). Body: serif (Times/Georgia-like), ~20pt, black, left-aligned wrapped paragraph with bold emphasis; 'same location' is bold AND dark red. In the bullets above, **...** marks bold. Diagram annotations use a handwriting-style font (Comic Sans/Segoe Print-like), black, ~16-18pt; the equation is in red in the same handwritten style using middle dots '·'. No numbered or bulleted lists; the paragraph is plain wrapped text.
animation_state: Slide appears fully revealed with no mid-build elements. The black strip at the very bottom is the video player's progress bar, not an animated slide element.
recreation_brief: 1. Create a 16:9 slide with a white background. 2. Draw a full-width rectangle across the top (~0-22% height), fill #E8E8E8, no outline. 3. Centered inside it, place the title 'How many filter can we apply on the image' in Arial Bold ~32pt, color #990000 (keep the singular 'filter' verbatim). 4. Below, draw a full-width rectangle (~24-45% height, ~2% side margins), fill #FFFFE1 with a thin black outline. 5. Inside it, Times New Roman ~20pt black, left-aligned, two lines: 'We can Apply multiple filters on the same location (e.g. 5 different filters on the same location.  For Example:' with 'multiple filters' bold black and 'same location' bold #990000; then '[ one to detect edges, one to detect lines, one to detect curves, ...etc)' with 'detect edges', 'detect lines', 'detect curves' bold black. 6. Draw a large rectangle covering ~46-95% of the slide height, white fill, 2pt #CC0000 border. 7. Inside-left, build the input image: a perspective parallelogram slab filled #D2691E with #8B4513 edges; add handwritten-style (Comic Sans/Segoe Print, black, ~16-18pt) labels 'RGB' above and '3 dims' at the left with a tiny arrow; draw a small circle containing 'X' on the slab; add two '7' labels with small arrows marking the patch extent; draw 4-5 horizontal dashed black lines from the slab toward the center. 8. In the center, draw five overlapping perspective slabs (front-row colors #30A0D0, #40B050, #E02020, #F0E020, #8040C0, with tan/gray/navy slabs partially visible behind); place handwritten '5' above with a small pointer and '3' below. 9. Place a large '=' between the stack and the cube. 10. On the right, draw a 3D cube (~2.2in) filled #E8C890 with darker #D9A85E top/side faces; place 5 circles along the top face (tan, tan, tan, dark brown, green) and 5 circles on the front face (#20B0A0, #40B050, #E02020, #F0E020, #8040C0); add handwritten 'Depth=5 dims' at its upper right and a plain black right-arrow pointing into the cube's upper-left. 11. At the bottom-left of the panel add handwritten-style black text 'How many weights for these 5 neurons?' (~20pt) and beneath it, in red #E02020, '5 · 7 · 7 · 3 = 735'. 12. Leave the bottom ~5% of the frame empty/black only if mimicking the video frame; the slide itself ends at the red-bordered panel.
